subject: FinEx — Throughput & SLO qualification follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finex-payments.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: FinEx — Throughput & SLO qualification follow-up

Hey Daniel / Aisha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps so we can size a Redwood Dedicated/Dedicated-like config for your production traffic. Please confirm or correct the numbers below and share any sample traffic you can (anonymized CSVs, p95/p99 from your proxy, or a short list of typical requests).

Summary of requirements (as I heard them):
- SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 200 ms for streaming responses; 99th percentile <= 500 ms for non-streaming API calls.
- Workload shapes:
  - Steady-state: ~150 QPS (requests/sec)
  - Peak: up to ~800 QPS sustained for short bursts (~10–20 minutes)
  - Average request size: ~120 tokens; long-tail requests up to ~800 tokens once every few hours
  - Concurrency target: ~100 concurrent streams (clients keeping streams open for a few hundred ms between chunks)
- Streaming: chunked responses (server push) are required for chat UX; we need ~50–100 ms token emission latency once the model starts streaming.

Derived throughput numbers (please verify):
- Steady-state token throughput ~18,000 tokens/sec (150 QPS * 120 tokens)
- Peak token throughput ~96,000 tokens/sec (800 QPS * 120 tokens) — note this increases if average tokens are higher during peaks

Open questions / asks from FinEx:
1) Can you confirm the accurate peak QPS and average/median tokens per request?
2) Do you have a distribution of request sizes (histogram) or a sample traffic dump we can use for load testing?
3) Any strict SLA windows (e.g., European market hours) or multi-region routing requirements?

Next steps we propose:
- You share 1 week of anonymized request logs or a sample CSV (we use this to generate a realistic replay for load testing).
- We run an initial capacity estimate and send back a suggested GPU pool config + expected p95/p99 numbers with batching/kv-caching assumptions.
- Schedule a 60-min sizing call to walk through the estimate and tradeoffs (batching vs latency vs unit cost).

I've attached a quick throughput-sizing template you can fill (finex_throughput_sizing_template.xlsx) and added a sample CSV file name suggestion. Happy to hop on a call Thursday or Friday next week.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Attachment: finex_throughput_sizing_template.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finex-payments.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Aisha Spencer <aisha.spencer@finex-payments.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinEx — Throughput & SLO qualification follow-up

Thanks Neha — this looks right overall. A few clarifications from our side:

- Peak: we typically see sustained peaks around 600–700 QPS for ~15 minutes during settlement spikes; very occasionally (1–2x per week) there are micro-peaks to ~1,200 QPS for a couple of minutes.
- Steady-state: our current baseline is closer to 200 QPS actually (we had a recent traffic growth) — apologies, I should have given the updated number in the call.
- Average tokens: median ~100 tokens; mean ~150 tokens due to a long tail.
- Long requests: ~0.5% of requests exceed 600 tokens.
- Streaming behavior: we stream tokens in chunks of ~16–32 tokens per chunk; client side expects first chunk within ~150–200 ms and subsequent chunks every 60–120 ms.

We can provide an anonymized 7-day traffic CSV (timestamp, path, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms) — I’ll drop that in the Drive folder you linked by EOD Thursday.

Also: can you include a rough unit-cost estimate (per 1M tokens) for both hosted and dedicated options in the sizing doc? That will help our procurement team.

—Daniel
Director of Engineering | FinEx Payments
daniel.park@finex-payments.com

Subject: Re: FinEx — Throughput & SLO qualification follow-up

Great context — thanks both. A couple of follow-ups from a sizing/architecture perspective:

1) Sizing heuristics (initial):
   - Given the updated steady-state ~200 QPS and median ~100 tokens, baseline token throughput ~20k tokens/sec.
   - For sustained peaks ~700 QPS -> ~70k tokens/sec; micro-peaks to 1.2k QPS -> ~144k tokens/sec (short bursts).

2) Concurrency and streaming considerations:
   - Streaming sessions hold concurrency longer; we should assume 100–150 concurrent open streams during peaks.
   - Continuous batching helps lower cost but increases first-token latency. We'll prototype a hybrid: small immediate push for first chunk (low-latency path) + batching for subsequent tokens.

3) Proposed action items:
   - Neha: once FinEx drops the 7-day anonymized CSV, we will run a traffic replay in a perf env to measure realistic p95/p99 under different batching/window settings.
   - Redwood infra: provide a preliminary config matrix (GPU types, estimated instances, expected p95/p99, token/sec capacity per pool, and cost estimate). I can take point on the first cut.
   - Load test: schedule a 2-hour spike test covering 1.2k QPS micro-burst plus a 20-minute 700 QPS sustained window.

4) Quick thresholds to validate in the test:
   - p95 end-to-end latency <= 200 ms for streaming first-chunk and <= 500 ms p99 for full-response non-streaming calls
   - Token emission latency for subsequent chunks <= 120 ms (this is important for the UX)

I'll draft the preliminary config and send it by end of day Friday so we can align before the load run. Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.inference.com
